items.new_information: 托管运行时这一新产品及自托管沙箱选项、与 ChatGPT Work 同底座

evidence.quote: OpenAI 推出基于 Codex 运行框架的托管式 Agents API 。OpenAI 推出了 Agents API，让开发者可以把会调用工具的智能体作为托管服务来构建和部署；它运行在 OpenAI 的 Codex harness 之上，并接管底层的智能体基础设施。该 API 围绕四个核心概念组织：Agent（模型、指令、工具与 MCP 服务器）、Environment（可选的沙箱或计算机，用于访问文件、加载技能、执行命令）、Session（持久化的智能体实例）以及 Events 与 items（会话中输入与输出的内容）。 这次发布意味着 OpenAI 进一步向技术栈上层延伸——从单纯售卖模型端点，转向提供一个完整的智能体运行时，这可能重塑开发者构建 AI 产品的方式，并加剧与 Anthropic 的

Claude Agent SDK 及其他 harness 的竞争。它同时也立刻引出两个问题：厂商锁定风险，以及“LLM 端点”与“智能体运行框架”之间的界限究竟在哪里。 这项托管服务打包了自动上下文压缩、多智能体编排、程序化工具调用以及对 MCP 的支持；OpenAI 还指出开发者可以选择自行托管沙箱——有评论者认为这一选项是抵御锁定风险的重要退路。由于该 harness 负责状态持久化与长时间运行的会话，这一抽象对多步骤、工具驱动的任务价值最大，而对单次问答式调用则意义有限。
Scaled agents on demand.
This is pretty much the infrastructure that runs under the hood for ChatGPT Work, all wrapped up in an API which you can use to get started in < 1 min. Happy building.

Today we're launching the Agents API, a brand new way to build Agents in the cloud, backed by the Codex harness. Bring along all your favorite tools and connectors, connect it to any sandbox, and let Astra cook.

evidence.quote: 这次站出来的是 Andreas Thom，德累斯顿工业大学几何学教授，长期研究 geometric group theory、sofic groups 等方向，本身就是这个问题最核心的专家之一。
OpenAI 在训练 Astra 时，可能吸收了他和数学家 Gábor Kun 使用 AI 讨论 Gromov soficity conjecture 时留下的内容，随后 Astra 又解决了高度相关的问题。
巧的是，OpenAI 8 月 1 日公布 Astra 的“十大数学突破”时，第 3 项正是构造出 non-sofic group，也就是解决这个研究了二十多年的核心问题。
OpenAI 最初发布时曾宣称这些问题“至少十年没有取得主要进展”，随后遭到数学界质疑。
OpenAI 后来修改了表述，并承认 non-sofic group 的证明“依赖重要的近期数学工作”，其中就包括 Kun 和 Thom 的研究。
更微妙的是，Kun 和 Thom 之后发表的论文也明确写道，他们的新工作“建立在 OpenAI 找到第一个 nonsofic group 的突破之上”。

evidence.quote: 🚨 On September 6, 2026, @Liquid_BTC was affected by a cache key collision vulnerability in rangeproof verification.

An attacker minted ~3,998.5 L-BTC with no corresponding peg-in. Within minutes, the unbacked L-BTC was pegged out into real BTC on the Bitcoin mainnet. About 3,400 BTC was later returned to the federation peg wallet, while ~598.5 BTC remains under the attacker’s control.

3️⃣ On a cache hit, nodes skipped secp256k1_rangeproof_verify and min-value checks, accepted an unbacked commitment, and minted ~3,998.5 L-BTC. The fake UTXOs were consolidated and pegged out within minutes.

⚙️ Root Cause: The Elements rangeproof cache key concatenated variable-length fields without length prefixes. Distinct argument tuples could hash to the same key, so a positive cache hit meant skipping cryptographic verification.

🛡️ SlowMist Insight: A positive-result cache in a consensus verification path is itself a cryptographic primitive. Every field the verifier reads — and every field boundary — must be unambiguously bound into the key. Treat cache-key integrity as a mandatory item in consensus-layer audits.

evidence.quote: TLDR: For most of financial history, executing a collective investment strategy required assets to be placed into a legally pooled vehicle controlled by a manager. Courts therefore came to treat shared management, proportional returns, and collective administration as evidence of a common enterprise.

Non-custodial, programmable smart contracts like vaults break that historical link. evidence.quote: Basically, Vitalik is proposing that Ethereum stop doing expensive cryptographic verification itself and instead outsource it to the network. Today, every signature or zero-knowledge proof gets checked onchain, which is slow, costly, and forces protocol politics whenever someone wants support for a new algorithm.
* Quantum-safe wallets become affordable.
* Privacy becomes cheap by default.

* Ultra-cheap quantum-safe privacy protocols. Status quo minimum cost for private txs is ~300k if you engineer very well (no one does), status quo quantum-safe is ~10M gas, this could reduce it to low tens of thousands.
Hence, the bandwidth load is bounded: each node's outbound is one STARK (~100-300 kB) per tick, plus each transaction getting broadcasted through the network once (as happens already).
Total onchain overhead: one STARK (100-300 kB), plus 96 bytes for each statement being proven.
EIP-8288 enables Ethereum to scale in a fourth dimension -- proof verification.

The problem with quantum-safe STARKs however is that they are very large (~512kb) and will therefore take millions of gas to verify.  Therefore, for Ethereum to support private, post-quantum transactions at scale, it's important to lower the cost of verifying STARKs.

The core insight of EIP-8288 is that we can solve these problems by aggregating signatures/proofs with a distributed network -- the mempool itself.  Each mempool node would locally aggregate proofs of the signatures/proofs it has seen, and instead of gossiping the raw signatures/proofs, it would gossip the aggregated proofs instead.  This new architecture
- Since mempool nodes gossip aggregated proofs rather than raw sigs/proofs, the bandwidth requirements on the mempool are vastly reduced.

items.author: EulerLagrange
items.event: 质疑线上KYC核验的可审计性
items.new_information: 给出输入不可验证导致下游全部不可信的论证结构

evidence.quote: My claim: the kind of verification Persona sells isn't auditable, even with the full codebase in front of you at any moment.

An audit replays a process against its inputs and confirms the output followed. Persona's inputs are a photo of an ID and a few frames of a face. Replay the code against them and the strongest thing you can conclude is that the software correctly judged these pixels look like a real document and a live person. It cannot verify someone’s actual identity.

Beyond genAI, anything collected client-side: device fingerprint, sensor data, the liveness signal itself cannot be trusted. Code running on the attacker's device can be swapped for code that reports whatever the attacker wants. The server can't verify the client ran honestly. It can only verify the client said it did.

https://t.co/kFc3S9lHLD - tools like Frida let you hijack and modify the functionality of any app while it’s running on a rooted Android or Jailbroken iPhone. Any detection of root/jb can itself be disabled with this.
If the inputs into a pipeline of auditable code can’t be verified, nothing downstream can.

evidence.quote: This is the AWS moment for agents.

OpenAI just shipped the Agents API, and everything that made agents hard to build is now something you rent instead of build. Keeping one running for days, remembering what it's doing, using tools, recovering when a step fails. Now it's an API call.

I'll be honest, my first reaction was that this is bad news for a lot of people I know. If your whole company is an agent platform, the thing you spent the last year building is now included for the price of tokens.

If the hardest engineering just became a line item, then the only thing left that's actually hard is knowing the job. Like what counts as a done claim, what makes a filing get rejected, where the money leaks.

So the wedge now is owning one painful workflow with your own tools, data, approvals, and a clear ROI. Freight exceptions, insurance reviews, security triage, revenue leakage, healthcare admin, compliance ops.

items.new_information: 把争点归为中间概念被黑箱化而非能力比较

evidence.quote: A lot of people are missing Terence Tao’s point and thinking “mathematicians are upset that AI is better than them.” That’s not what he’s saying, and some people are forgetting that Tao is one of the most AI-pilled mathematicians out there.

His point is that when people work on discovering something, along the way they invent new concepts. Those concepts later become useful far beyond the original goal, and enables further inventions. Finding a solution does matter, but the intermediate idea is often what makes the field richer, because other people can share it and build the next thing from
Terence’s worry is that a machine automating a solution robs the field of the value of developing the intermediate discoveries in the pursuit of larger discoveries.

In other words: pure ‘solution extraction’ that hides the process of discovery can leave the field with a checked-off theorem but little new insight or new questions to pursue. And it might prevent us from understanding a field deeper.

So the question is not “is AI allowed to solve hard problems?” It is “in this field (math, science, tech, etc.), is the answer itself the main point, or are the concepts and abstractions we use to get there also the thing we need to maintain?”​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

But back to Reserve. They just completed two rounds of audits without any critical findings (those audits were co-funded by @UniswapFND btw), and have announced the genesis charter mint to take place on 14th of September.

The Standard Reserve is an onchain central bank with its own currency ($STANDARD), one market (a hooked ETH/STANDARD pool on Uniswap v4), and one signal metric (net $ETH flow through that pool) that defines the monetary policy.
The v4 hook on the liq pool counts $ETH in via buys minus $ETH out via sells each epoch. That net number is the sole determinant of the monetary regime:
- Net inflow = expansion: the issuance multiplier steps up one notch per epoch (raises must be earned) and fees route to the expansion vault, which buys tokenized gold as a hard reserve.

- Net outflow = contraction: the multiplier gets cut immediately and fees flip to the contraction vault, which buys $STANDARD on the pool and burns all of it in hourly rate-limited ticks capped near 5% of pool depth per day (automated buy and burn against sell pressure).
The Standard Reserve is coming on September 14.
